evals.prompt: Support agents want to search tasks by their project's name.
evals.expected_output: A stored `text` mirror `project_name` on `task`, in `searchableFields: ['name', 'project_name']`; a `beforeInsert` / `beforeUpdate` hook on `task` stamps it, an `afterUpdate` hook on `project` re-stamps it on rename; rows written outside hooks get a backfill.

evals.prompt: Sales reps see only their own leads, sales managers their unit and everything below it; every signed-in user reads the `product` catalog.
evals.expected_output: `lead` is `sharingModel: 'private'`; the rep grant carries `readScope: 'own'`, the manager grant `readScope: 'unit_and_below'` (`@objectstack/security-enterprise` + `requires: ['hierarchy-security']`, else fails closed to `own`); `product` is `sharingModel: 'public_read'`.

evals.prompt: Expose the `customers` table of our Postgres reporting database as a read-only `legacy_customer` object.
evals.expected_output: A `defineDatasource` entry (say `reporting`) with `schemaMode: 'external'` (the remote schema stays unaltered) and no credential in the declaration: the password is read at connect from `OS_DATASOURCE_REPORTING_PASSWORD` (the name upper-cased) while the host switch `OS_DATASOURCE_ENV_CREDENTIALS` is `on` (`os serve`/`start`/`dev` default it on); the object sets `datasource: 'reporting'` and `external: { remoteName: 'customers', columnMap }`; the write gate stays closed (no `allowWrites`, no `writable`).

evals.prompt: Seed the `country` table for every environment; add demo `opportunity` rows (dev/test only) closing 45 days after install, owned by the installer, and refreshed from the seed on every replay except `stage`: a nightly job advances it, and a replay must not reset it.
evals.expected_output: `defineSeed(Country, { externalId: 'code', mode: 'upsert', records })` for reference data; `defineSeed(Opportunity, { mode: 'upsert', env: ['dev', 'test'], ... })` for the refreshed demo rows — natural-key lookups, CEL values (`close_date: cel`daysFromNow(45)``, `owner_id: cel`os.user.id``), parents first; `columns: { stage: { applyOn: 'create' } }` so the `upsert` replay leaves the job-owned column (the `ignore` default would refresh nothing).

evals.prompt: Finance may edit a contract's legal terms (`governing_law`, `liability_cap`) while it is a draft, not once approved, signing or active; legal still edits them.
evals.expected_output: Row-conditioned field permission entries on the finance set — `'clm_contract.governing_law': { readable: true, editable: false, when: "status in ['approved', 'signing', 'active']" }`, likewise `liability_cap`; legal keeps its edit grant.

evals.prompt: Portal users may read only the orders of the accounts they belong to, never another account's.
evals.expected_output: On the roster object `account_member` (`user` + `account` lookup): `membershipKeys: { portal_account_ids: { userField: 'user', valueField: 'account' } }`; a portal permission set reads it (`using: 'account in current_user.portal_account_ids'`), a position names it in `permissionSets`, portal staff join on the `external` tier outside the `everyone` baseline. No policy per account, no owner stamp per order.

evals.prompt: We serve English and Chinese users. An `order` whose `amount` exceeds its account's `credit_limit` must not save; API clients branch on `CREDIT_LIMIT`, a zh-CN rep reads `超出账户信用额度`.
evals.expected_output: A `beforeInsert` / `beforeUpdate` hook on `order` declares `refusals: { CREDIT_LIMIT: { message: 'Over the account credit limit.' } }`; its sandboxed `body: { language: 'js', source }` reads the account via `ctx.api` and refuses by code only (`throw Object.assign(new Error(), { code: 'CREDIT_LIMIT' })`); the zh-CN bundle's `hooks: { <hook>: { refusals: { CREDIT_LIMIT: { message: '超出账户信用额度' } } } }` is served in the caller's locale; a catalogue on a hook without a `js` body is refused at save.

evals.prompt: Web-form leads arrive ownerless; inside sales holds them until a rep takes one, and two reps must never own the same lead.
evals.expected_output: `queues: [defineQueue({ name: 'crm_inside_sales', label: 'Inside Sales', members: [{ type: 'position', value: 'crm_inside_sales_rep' }] })]` and an `assignmentRules` entry `assignTo: { type: 'queue', value: 'crm_inside_sales' }` with no `strategy` park each lead in the injected `queue` column; a rep claims by an ordinary by-id `{ owner_id: <self> }` update, the loser gets `409 CONCURRENT_UPDATE`.

evals.prompt: A `vendor` list view of the rows whose `api_key` (a `secret` field) starts with `sk_live`.
evals.expected_output: Redirects: a credential is filtered only by presence, `filter: [{ field: 'api_key', operator: 'is_not_null' }]`; any other filter or sort is `400 INVALID_FIELD`.

evals.prompt: An `account` whose `tax_id` appears in our `blocked_tax_id` object must not save, on create or edit. Our tax authority also offers a lookup API; can the same hook call it?
evals.expected_output: A `beforeInsert` / `beforeUpdate` hook on `account` with a sandboxed `body: { language: 'js', source, capabilities: ['api.read'] }`: the source returns when the write carries no `tax_id`, reads `ctx.api.object('blocked_tax_id').findOne({ where: { tax_id: ctx.input.tax_id } })` and throws when it finds a row. Not a validation rule (there is no `custom` / `async` type) and not the deprecated inline `handler`. The tax-authority API is not called from the hook: a `body` has no outbound HTTP, so that check goes through a Connector recipe.

evals.prompt: Expose the remote `suppliers` table of our `warehouse` datasource as a read-only `ext_supplier` object every member can read.
evals.expected_output: A complete `ObjectSchema.create` with `datasource: 'warehouse'`, `external: { remoteName: 'suppliers' }` and an authored `sharingModel: 'public_read'` — a publish with none is refused (`security-owd-unset`), and on 'private' a member reads no row of a binding whose remote rows carry no owner.

evals.prompt: When an `account`'s `industry` changes, copy the new value into `account_industry` on every contact of that account.
evals.expected_output: An `afterUpdate` hook on `account` with a sandboxed `body: { language: 'js', source, capabilities: ['api.write'] }`: the source compares `ctx.input.industry` with `ctx.previous.industry` and, when it changed, makes one bulk write, `ctx.api.object('contact').update({ account_industry: ctx.input.industry }, { where: { account_id: ctx.previous.id }, multi: true })`. The row is keyed on `ctx.previous.id`: a body's `ctx.input` carries `id` only when the payload does, so on a bulk or by-`where` update the key would be empty and the `where` would match every contact. Not the deprecated inline `handler`, and not a bulk method the hook's `ctx.api` does not have (`updateMany` throws "not implemented").

evals.prompt: Run our `account` enrichment hook only for accounts whose `annual_revenue` (an optional currency field) is above 1,000,000.
evals.expected_output: The hook's declarative `condition: P`record.annual_revenue != null && record.annual_revenue > 1000000``. `record` is total over the declared fields, so an empty `annual_revenue` reads `null` and CEL has no `>` overload for it: the publish gate refuses the unguarded comparison, and at runtime it would refuse each write on an account with no `annual_revenue`. `has(record.annual_revenue)` is not a guard (a declared field holding null is present).
